Learned AGA has filed counter affidavit, same is taken on record.

This is second bail application.
First bail application has been rejected by Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh, J. for want of prosecution vide order dated 1.11.2022.

Since the Hon'ble Judge, who has rejected the first bail application, is presently not sitting at Lucknow, therefore, in terms of administrative order of Hon'ble Acting Chief Justice dated 13.11.2018, this bail application has been put up before the regular Court.

As per learned counsel for the applicant the present applicant is in jail since 27.9.2021 in Case Crime No. 345 of 2021 u/s 376, 506, 420 of IPC & 3(1),5(1) & 8(5) of U.P. Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, 2021, P.S. Colonelganj, District Gonda.
Attention has been drawn towards the impugned F.I.R. wherein for the allegation in question the entire family of the present applicant has been implicated.

sentences.text: Precisely, the allegation against the present applicant is that by adopting fraudulent tactics and threatening for dire consequences the applicant with the help of his parents got the religion of the daughter of the informant converted from Hindu religion to Islam religion and got married, thereafter established physical religion with her.
The statement of the girl / prosecutrix has been recorded u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. (Annexure no. 6 and 7) wherein she has supported the prosecution version as stated in the F.I.R.

As per learned counsel at the time of her examination before the learned trial court as P.W.-3 she has supported the prosecution version in her chief-examination but in her cross-examination, which was conducted on the same dated i.e. 30.11.2022, she did not support the prosecution version, rather she stated that the present applicant or his family members have not forced her to convert the religion from Hindu to Islam.
She is still Hindu by religion.
In her cross-examination she has stated that she has denied for medical examination.
She never went to the Collectorate for getting the papers prepared regarding her conversion.
Her father is serving on the post of Home Guard at P.S. Colonelganj.

Therefore, the learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that when the prosecutrix has not supported the prosecution story at the time of her cross-examination and has stated that the present applicant or his family members have not committed any offence against her, the present applicant may be enlarged on bail.

He has also informed that the prosecutrix being a 'star witness' has already been examined and one eye-witness namely, Amresh Singh has been examined, therefore, if he is released on bail he would not influence the witnesses which are formal in nature.
Further, he shall cooperate in the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order.

Per contra, Sri Alok Saran, learned AGA has stated that one Amar Singh (witness no. 3) and Smt.
Seema Singh who is mother of the prosecutrix (witness no. 8), who are eye witnesses, are yet to be examined, therefore, unless and until those eye witnesses are examined the present applicant may not be released on bail.
Learned AGA has also stated that eye-witness Amresh Singh has supported the prosecution version and has stated that the present applicant has committed offence as alleged in the F.I.R.

Sri Saran, learned AGA has demonstrated the statement u/s 161 Cr.P.C. of one Advocate namely,
Manoj Kumar Mishra s/o Devi Prasad Mishra, who is a practicing lawyer at Colonelganj, Gonda Niyaj Ahmad vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

2 recorded on 28.10.2021, wherein the Advocate has clearly stated that he is a practicing Advocate in the Civil Court.

On 23.9.2021 the accused-applicant along with his parents and one lady who was in 'Burka' approached him and had requested him to prepare one consent letter / affidavit on stamp paper for conversion of that girl to the religion of Islam and he prepared that consent letter /
affidavit.
However, later on he came to know that by means of that conversion the present applicant converted one Hindu girl to Islam religion, therefore, those persons may be punished as per law.
As per the Advocate, had he been known the aforesaid fact, he would have not been instrumental in preparing such documents.

Therefore, Sri Alok Saran, learned AGA has stated that the reliance on the cross-examination of the prosecutrix may not support the present applicant inasmuch as the Advocate has himself stated before the police that he had prepared the relevant documents regarding conversion of the prosecutrix from Hindu religion to Islam religion.

Besides, the chief-examination and cross-examination of the prosecutrix was conducted on the same date i.e. 30.11.2022 and in her chief-examination she has admitted the fact that she had given her earlier statement before the Magistrate u/s 164 Cr.P.C. and said statement given before the Magistrate was admitted by her,
meaning thereby whatever she had stated before the Magistrate may not be disbelieved only on the basis of of her cross-examination.
Sri Saran has also submitted that the learned trial court may consider the statements of all the witnesses including all the material available on record to arrive at any logical conclusion.
The contents of cross-examination of the prosecutrix may not be considered in isolation.

Since two eye-witness, one of them is mother of the prosecutrix are yet to be examined, therefore, at this stage the present applicant may not be released on bail, however, the direction may be issued to expedite the trial.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the material available on record including the original copy of the case diary, I am of the considered opinion that the learned trial court may arrive at any appropriate and lawful conclusion after considering complete material in its entirety including the statement of all the witnesses, more particularly the fact / material witnesses.

The submission of Sri Saran is correct to the effect that the statement of the prosecutrix during her cross-examination may not be considered in isolation, rather it shall be considered keeping in view her chief-examination as well as the statement of other witnesses.

Two fact / material witnesses,
who are the eye-witnesses namely, Sri Amar Singh and Smt. Seema Singh are yet to be examined and if need be the examination of the Advocate may be directed by the learned trial court on the request of learned counsel for the parties, therefore, this is not an appropriate stage to grant the bail to the present applicant, rather direction may be issued to expedite the trial and to expedite the examination of witnesses.
Therefore, without entering into the merits of the issue and considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, the bail application is liable to be rejected.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.

one eye-witness namely, Amar Singh, (witness no. 3) and Smt. Seema Singh (witness no. 8) who are eye-witnesses.

Remaining witnesses as per charge-sheet from serial no. 5 to 10 except Smt. Seema Singh are the formal witnesses, therefore, learned trial court is directed to examine all the remaining witnesses, more particularly, the aforesaid witnesses with expedition preferably within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order of this Court by fixing short dates and if any of the witnesses does not cooperate in the trial proceedings, the learned trial court may take appropriate coercive steps strictly in accordance with law but in any case all the remaining fact witnesses shall be finally examined within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order of this Court.
If all the witnesses are examined in the meantime, the trial court may conclude the trial and pass final order.

I am unable to comprehend when there is specific provision in the Cr.P.C. to conduct the trial on day to day basis in serious offences like the present case, as to why the trial is not being conducted and concluded in terms of such provisions.

The liberty is given to the learned counsel for the applicant to file another bail application, if the aforesaid witnesses are not examined in terms of order of this Court as the said ground may be considered as a fresh ground.
.
(Rajesh Singh Chauhan, J.) Order Date :- 19.1.2023
